title: Composable Privilege Fabric and Permission Provenance for RBAC v2
creator: Priya Shah
description: Design and spec a composable RBAC v2 model that encodes privileges as reusable capability bundles, supports permission provenance tracing for audit logs, integrates with SSO/SAML group assertions, and provides admin controls (breakglass, transient elevation, role delegation). Deliverables: data model, enforcement contracts, migration plan from RBAC v1, audit hook points, and a minimal prototype evaluation service.
acceptance_criteria: Data model defined with resource hierarchy, scope semantics, and composable capability bundles (JSON schema + examples)
Permission evaluation algorithm specified with complexity bounds and caching strategy (including invalidation rules)
Mapping rules for SAML/SSO group claims to role bindings documented, including edge cases for overlapping assertions
Audit provenance model defined so each granted/denied decision can be traced to binders (role, group, token, delegated grant) and persisted in audit logs
Migration plan from RBAC v1 with rolling upgrade steps, backward compatibility guarantees, and monitoring playbook
Prototype enforcement service (beta) that can answer check(resource, action, principal) and return provenance metadata within 200ms p95 for typical workloads
tasks: Finalize capability bundle format and canonical permission names (Marco)
Define resource hierarchy primitives (tenant / org / project / runtime / model) and scope resolution rules (Priya)
Spec permission evaluation API and caching contract (Eng-Infra)
Document SAML/SSO claim to role-binding translation and admin UX flows for group sync (Identity team)
Design audit event schema for provenance fields and retention mapping to Console/Observability (SRE)
Build prototype enforcement service and unit tests (ENG backend)
Create migration automation scripts and backward-compat validation checks (Data Migrations)
Security review and threat model workshop (Security)
Run perf bench with real-ish workload and collect p95 latency, cache hit rates, and DB load (Perf)
Draft rollout plan and incident playbook for mis-graded permissions (oncall + PM)
decisions: Use composable capability bundles (named lists of granular permissions) instead of free-form DSL to simplify audits and enforcement caching
Permission evaluation returns provenance metadata (source_binding, binding_type, evaluated_at) to support auditability and explainability
Store role bindings in a denormalized materialized view for fast reads; authoritative source remains normalized tables updated by transactional migrations
Transient admin elevation implemented as short-lived delegation tokens issued by the control plane with explicit justification field to be recorded in audit logs
tradeoffs: Capability bundles vs DSL: bundles simplify caching and permission matrix UIs but are less expressive for conditional logic (e.g., time-based allow). We prioritize operational simplicity for first rollout.
Denormalized reads improve p95 latency but increase write complexity and migration risk; mitigated by strict migration choreography and shadow writes during rollout.

Including provenance metadata in every evaluation increases audit log size and slightly impacts latency; we will make provenance optional in high-throughput internal checks and required for all external-facing admin decisions.
